grants.title: GO8341: Modernised Multicultural Grants Program: Infrastructure for Multicultural Communities
grants.summary: Assessment and notification of outcomes will be divided into 2 batches. The table below identifies the cut-off dates for each batch: Batch 1 - closes 4:00 pm AEST on 18 May 2026 - ID 2025-5201 - Closed Batch 2 - closes 4:00 pm AEDT on 12 November 2026 - ID 2026-6462 - Open. The Australian Government is inviting organisations through an open competitive process to apply to deliver community infrastructure under the Infrastructure for Multicultural Communities program from 2026–27. The Infrastructure for Multicultural Communities grant opportunity provides total funding of up to $41.6 million (GST exclusive) for construction, upgrade or extension of infrastructure. You can apply for one of 3 streams of grant funding based on the type of infrastructure project and amount of grant funding you require for the project. The grant opportunity is comprised of 2 funding opportunities, called batches. You can apply for funding in one batch. Batch 1 opens on 7 April 2026 and closes on 18 May 2026. Batch 2 opens on 18 May 2026 and closes on 12 November 2026. The following groups and projects will be prioritised for funding: new and emerging multicultural communities, as defined below projects focussed on achieving positive outcomes for multicultural women, multicultural LGBTIQA+ community members, and multicultural people with a disability. Co-contributions are required towards the value of your project and the minimum amount of co funding is determined by whether you are applying as a priority group/project or other. The objectives of the grant opportunity are to: deliver physical infrastructure to support multicultural communities connect and commune in a designated physical environment provide co-funding to deliver community-focussed infrastructure and amenities provide infrastructure and amenities that benefit the wider multicultural community by improving equity and social inclusion.

grants.title: GO8220: Saluting their Service Commemorative Grants Program 2026–27
grants.summary: Assessment and notification of outcomes will be into 2 batches. The table below identifies the cut-off dates for all 2 batches: Batch 1 - closes 9:00 PM AEST on 29 July 2026 - ID 2025-5415 - Closed Batch 2 - closes 9:00 PM AEDT 21 January 2027 - ID 2025-5416 - Open. The Australian Government is inviting eligible organisations to apply for grant funding under the Saluting Their Service Commemorative Grants Program (STS program). The objective of the STS Program is to commemorate the service and sacrifice of Australia’s service personnel who served in wars, conflicts and peace operations, including National Service personnel, and their families. The intended outcome of the STS Program is to provide funding for projects and activities that: promote appreciation and understanding of the experiences of service, and the role of service personnel preserve, add to the sum of knowledge on, or provide access to information about Australia’s wartime heritage. 1. Community Grants Grants up to $10,000 are available for projects and activities that: are focused on the local community commemorate the service and sacrifice of local community members are primarily accessed by the local community. 2. Major Grants Grants between $10,001 and $150,000 are available for major commemorative projects and activities that are significant from a national, state, territory and/or broader regional perspective. These projects may include the construction of new war or peace memorials where none currently exist, as well as additions to existing memorials. If your project relates to restoring or changing a memorial or other commemorative artefact, there may be heritage and conservation considerations.

grants.title: GO8482: Long-term Trials of Drought Resilient Farming Practices Program Round 3
grants.summary: The Australian Government, through the Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry (the Department), invites applications for grants, through a targeted competitive process, under the Future Drought Fund Long-term Trials of Drought Resilient Farming Practices Program Round 3 (the Program). The Program builds on the success of the existing Long-term Trials Rounds 1 and 2, which are delivering projects to investigate innovative and transformational cropping, grazing, horticulture and mixed farming practices through the lens of drought resilience and associated risk management. The Program objectives remain the same as previous rounds, to investigate innovative farming practices and technologies through evidence-based trials to inform farmers, and foster transformational change to build economic, environmental and social resilience to drought and climate variability. The Program will support extensions to existing trials under the Long-term Trials Round 1 program and new projects from the recommended but unfunded applicants to the Long-term Trials Round 1 and Round 2 programs. Projects will commence from 2026–27. Up to $20 million (GST exclusive) is available over 4 years, with a minimum of $2 million and a maximum of $5 million per project. Projects must use robust, scientific trials to test, refine, and demonstrate the effectiveness of practices and technologies. This evidence-based approach is designed to support and drive adoption by providing farmers with the confidence to apply new techniques on farm and at scale. Larger and longer-term projects are encouraged to deliver lasting change.

grants.title: GO8521: Carer Peak Body Organisational Support and National Carers Week
grants.summary: The Carers Peak Body Organisation Support and National Carers Week programs (the programs) will run over 5 years from 2026-27 to 2030-31. The program is a continuation of the Carer Peak Bodies and National Carers Week program (2019-25). It provides organisation support for peak representation of carers and their interests as representatives. The program would receive funding of $4,725,000 (indexed) to continue to provide organisation support for peak representation of carers and their interests as representatives into 2030-31. The purpose of this grant opportunity is twofold: to represent the Australian Government as the National Carers Peak Body and to deliver on the objectives of both the Carers Peak Body Organisation Support and National Carers Week programs. Expected outcomes include improved policies and services, greater recognition of carers, increased community awareness, stronger engagement, and better access to supports. To view the grant opportunity documents, please select the red "Grant Opportunity Documents" button on the left-hand side.

grants.title: GO8520: Carer Inclusive Workplace Initiative
grants.summary: The Carer Inclusive Workplace Initiative Program (the program) will run over 2 years from 2026-27 to 2027-28. This grant program supports the Australian Government’s contribution to outcomes for Disability and Carers by advancing the objectives of Program 4.1 - Disability and Carers. The objective of the grant opportunity is to assist and encourage employers to develop and adopt practices that encourages and support employees with caring responsibilities. The purpose of this grant opportunity is to expand carer inclusivity in workplaces around Australia. It will enable businesses, in particular small businesses, to self-identify as a carer inclusive organisation without the time commitment and cost associated with a full accreditation process. To view the grant opportunity documents, please select the red "Grant Opportunity Documents" button on the left-hand side.

grants.title: GO8552: 2026-27 Grants in Aid Program
grants.summary: The Australian Government is inviting national ex-service organisations (ESOs) through a closed non-competitive process to apply to deliver services under the Grants in Aid (GIA) Program, which forms part of Program 2.4 Veterans’ Community Care and Support. The 2026-27 GIA Program aims to support the role of national ESOs to provide coordinating and representational support for the Australian veteran and Defence community. This program is open to national ESOs by invitation and provides funding to encourage cooperation and communication between the ex-service community, ESOs and the Australian Government. Funding for national ESOs aims to encourage the national advancement of the objectives of ESOs. The objective of the grant opportunity is to fund discrete projects or activities by national ESOs that address a specific problem or issue and achieve a clear benefit to the ex-service and Defence community. The intended outcomes of the program are to: · assist national ESOs to support their branches, sub-branches and affiliated organisations in performing compensation and/or wellbeing advocacy or wellbeing support work · assist national ESOs to advance the objectives of all ESOs more generally · assist national ESOs to improve co-operation and communication between national bodies, branches, sub-branches and affiliated organisations on repatriation and military compensation matters · encourage co-operation and communication between the ex-service community, ESOs and the Australian Government.

grants.title: GO8505: Rural Health Multidisciplinary Training Program (2027-2031)
grants.summary: The purpose of this grant opportunity is to encourage, prepare and support health students (including First Nations students) to pursue health careers in MMM 2-7 areas of Australia through training, recruitment, selection, education, and research activities which are innovative, agile, and in line with available evidence on improved rural health workforce recruitment and retention. The Rural Health Multidisciplinary Training Program (RHMT) supports health students to undertake rural training through a network of rural clinical schools, university departments of rural health, dental faculties offering extended rural placements, and end-to-end rural medical training arrangements. The RHMT also supports regional training hubs, which build medical training pathways within a region and guide students and trainees through these. The aim of the RHMT is to improve the recruitment and retention of health professionals in rural and remote Australia. The Government has announced RHMT reforms to strengthen rural workforce outcomes, consolidate funding streams, improve delivery and reduce administrative burden. The reformed RHMT will: • shift to an outcomes-focused model for rural retention and workforce shortages • strengthen universities’ roles in meeting local and national workforce needs • encourage innovation and agility • remove outdated requirements and focus on longer-term outcomes • support continuous improvement across the RHMT network • reduce red tape and administrative burden • enhance qualitative and quantitative reporting • provide greater funding certainty to universities. Note: Please refer to Program FAQs, Briefing Session Recording, Transcript and Slide Presentation published on 11 August 2026. To view the grant opportunity documents, please select the red "Grant Opportunity Documents" button on the left-hand side.

grants.title: GO8444: Discovery Indigenous for funding commencing in 2027
grants.summary: The Discovery Indigenous scheme provides grant funding to support research projects conducted by Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander researchers. The Discovery Indigenous scheme objectives are to: support the retention of excellent Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander researchers in higher education institutions to expand research capacity in Australia; support excellent pure basic, strategic basic and applied research and research training, across all disciplines excluding clinical and other medical research, by Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander researchers as individuals and as teams; enhance the scale and focus of research in Australian Government priority areas and create economic, commercial, environmental, social and/or cultural benefits for Australia; and support national and international research collaboration. The intended outcomes of the Discovery Indigenous scheme are: an expanded knowledge base and research capacity in Australia; and economic, commercial, environmental, social and/or cultural benefits for Australia.

grants.title: GO8524: Great Barrier Reef Marine Debris Management and Mitigation Round 2
grants.summary: The Australian Government is inviting organisations in an open process to apply to deliver services under this grant opportunity. Objectives of the Round 2 grant opportunity are to: deliver large scale management and reduction of the threat of marine debris to species such as coral, turtles, dugongs and seabirds mitigate negative impacts of marine debris on tourism, recreation and fishing (commercial and recreational) within the Reef support activities that reduce water pollution from urban sources within Reef catchments improve water quality through the removal of marine debris from Reef coastlines and urban waterways develop and deliver targeted education and awareness raising activities to reduce and prevent litter, including plastics, from entering Reef waterways encourage greater community stewardship and involvement, including with First Nations peoples, promoting a shared sense of responsibility for Reef pollutants inform and contribute to wider plastic management and mitigation strategic policy for state and/or national scale implementation identify and support local or regional opportunities in circular or renewable material economies and/or activities.

grants.title: GO8516: Mobile Black Spot Program - West Coast Tasmania Mobile Capacity Uplift Round
grants.summary: The Mobile Black Spot Program West Coast Tasmania Mobile Capacity Uplift Round (the Round) will provide grant funding of up to $9.8 million (GST exclusive) to boost mobile coverage and capacity in the Local Government Areas of Circular Head, Waratah-Wynyard, and West Coast on the west coast of Tasmania. Eligible grant activities include upgrades to mobile base stations and backhaul networks, and construction of new mobile base stations. This grant opportunity is funded under the Australian Government’s Better Connectivity Plan for Regional and Rural Australia.

grants.title: GO8269: DRIVEN - Charger Grant Stream
grants.summary: The DRIVEN Charger Grant Stream grant opportunity makes $20 million available for the installation of new, public, fast EV charging stations at automotive dealership and EV repairer premises and, in turn, bolsters Australia’s public fast charger network. The objectives of the DRIVEN Charger Grant Stream are to: deliver charging stations at automotive dealership and EV repairer premises encourage installation of charging stations in regional areas of Australia support automotive dealerships and EV repairers looking to host charging stations facilitate partnerships between Australian automotive dealerships or EV repairers and EV charging businesses (e.g. Charge Point Operators). Register of interested site hosts To assist potential applicants, the Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water (DCCEEW) will facilitate a registration of interest process for potential site hosts (dealerships and EV repairers) interested in hosting charging stations. This register is intended to support partnership development and help applicants identify suitable sites for their projects. Use of the register is not mandatory and applicants may still identify suitable sites and site hosts not contained in the register. Access the DRIVEN Public EV Charging - Site Host Registration of Interest.

grants.title: GO8557: Gender Equality in Music Initiative
grants.summary: The Gender Equality in Music Initiative grant provides an opportunity to support targeted, practical activities that build safer and more inclusive industry settings, strengthen pathways for women into creative and technical roles, improve women’s access to leadership and professional development, and help shape a music industry that better reflects the diversity of the Australian community. The grant contributes to the vision of Working for Women: A Strategy for Gender Equality: an Australia where people are safe, treated with respect, have choices, and have access to resources and equal outcomes no matter their gender. By supporting targeted action in the music industry, the grant aligns most strongly with the priority areas of gender-based violence, economic equality and security, and leadership, representation and decision-making. The intended grant outcomes are: · Increased visibility and recognition of women in all their diversity across the Australian music industry · Improved pathways for women in all their diversity into paid work, professional networks, mentoring and leadership opportunities, particularly in male-dominated technical, production and programming roles · A safer and more inclusive industry that supports participation without discrimination, harassment or exclusion · Improved access to sector-level intersectional gender disaggregated data and practical tools to support gender equality outcomes in recruitment, programming and industry accountability · Strengthened cultural leadership and national visibility for First Nations women artists, musicians, producers and storytellers, including those from regional and remote communities.

grants.title: GO8549: Intensive Employment Services
grants.summary: As part of its employment services reform, the Australian Government is inviting organisations via a restricted process to apply to deliver the early roll out of an Intensive Employment Service. The Intensive Employment Service is for people with complex and interconnected barriers to employment, who have been unemployed for a significant period, may need additional support to build their confidence, capacity and capability and progress towards and into a job. The program will test and refine the delivery of an intensive service model with wraparound support, ahead of a proposed national rollout. The objectives of the program are to: test and refine an intensive service model that provides tailored, wraparound support delivered by skilled mentors to support people with diverse and intersecting employment challenges into employment improve participants’ confidence, capacity and capability to progress towards employment strengthen links between employment assistance and complementary supports that address barriers to participation in employment and work readiness generate evidence about effective service settings, delivery approaches and enabling conditions for future employment services reform support shared learning across grantees through a community of practice to inform continuous improvement and future service design.

grants.title: GO8531: Revive Live - Round 3
grants.summary: The Australian Government’s National Cultural Policy Revive recognises the importance of the live music sector and is increasing the support for the music industry. The Revive Live program was announced as part of the Government’s Critical Support for the Live Music and Festivals measure in the 2024/25 Federal Budget. The Government provided a further $25 million to extend the program for an additional two years to 30 June 2027. Revive Live will provide essential support to established live music venues and Australian music festivals to assist them to continue to operate in the current operating climate, limiting venue closures and event cancellations, and stimulating long-term sustainability. Revive Live will also have a focus on improving accessibility for disabled artists and patrons. Revive Live will: Increase performance opportunities including the development and discoverability of original contemporary music by Australian artists support a sustainable Australian live music ecosystem, allowing established live music venues to continue operating, and avoiding cancellation of Australian music festivals support stability in live music venues and music festivals, building resilience to change and risk, safety, inclusivity and representative programming improve accessibility at live music venues and music festivals, providing participation opportunities for audiences with disability as well as career pathways for musicians and music workers with disability. Revive Live will run from 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2027, with a total of $12.5 million available in 2026-27. The maximum grant amount is $150,000 for venues and small festivals, and larger festivals with more than 10,000 attendees can receive funding of up to $250,000

grants.title: GO8139: First Nations Clean Energy Advice Grants Round 1
grants.summary: The First Nations Clean Energy Advice Grants Round 1 was announced as part of the implementation of the Government’s First Nations Clean Energy Strategy. The objectives of the program are to support First Nations communities to participate in clean energy development and: build clean energy project skills and knowledge access technical and professional support make informed decisions as per principles of Free, Prior and Informed Consent (FPIC). The intended outcomes of the program are for First Nations communities to gain increased: access to technical and professional support confidence in engagement with clean energy developers and clean energy development opportunities collaboration and engagement with the clean energy industry clean energy project skills and knowledge participation in clean energy projects benefits from participation in clean energy development. Round 1 of the program will run from 2025-26 to 2026-27.

grants.title: GO8527: WA Roadmap Implementation Fund: Farm System Productivity Program
grants.summary: The program was announced as part of the $5.0 million WA Roadmap Implementation Fund in support of the recommendations in the WA Sheep Industry Roadmap to 2028 (the Roadmap)(www.thefutureflock.com.au/wa-roadmap-to-2028). The Roadmap sets out a forward-looking plan to guide Western Australia’s (WA) sheep industry transition away from live sheep exports by sea. Developed by industry and informed by extensive consultation, it identifies key challenges and opportunities and outlines a clear, practical path for growth, innovation and sustainability. The Roadmap outlines strategies and initiatives to address these challenges and opportunities, guiding future development, investment and collaboration. The program targets opportunities identified in the Roadmap and supports projects that are aligned with the strategies and initiatives identified in the Roadmap against the three goals: The whole supply chain operating efficiently to optimise market value and profitability Informed, confident decision-making across the industry A vibrant, positive and collaborative industry culture The program will consider a broad range of project proposals from the not-for-profit and commercial sectors to improve productivity, profitability and industry collaboration in implementing the Roadmap. Successful project proposals will demonstrate benefit to the broader WA sheep industry. The objective of this grant opportunity is: To assist sheep producers affected by the phase out of live sheep exports by sea by supporting projects that will enhanceon-farm systems and productivity, improve whole of supply chain profitability, and support a more collaborative industry culture. The intended outcome of this grant opportunity is: To improve confidence and productivity in farm systems as sheep producers adjust to changing markets and transition away from live sheep exports by sea.

grants.title: GO8511: Round 3 – Closing the Gap – Major Capital Works Program – 2026-27
grants.summary: For this grant opportunity, up to $180 million is available over two years (2026–27 to 2027–28). The funding aims to strengthen the Aboriginal Community Controlled Health Service (ACCHS) sector through improved infrastructure, including new and upgraded health clinics and associated housing for health professionals. Two funding rounds totalling $210 million have already been delivered under the Closing the Gap Major Capital Works (MCW) Program (Round 1 through GO5504 and Round 2 through GO6522). The current round represents Round 3 of the Closing the Gap MCW Program. To view the grant opportunity documents, please select the red "Grant Opportunity Documents" button on the left-hand side.

grants.title: GO8560: Indigenous Broadcasting and Media Program – Strengthening Community Broadcasting Grant Opportunity
grants.summary: The Indigenous Broadcasting and Media Program – Strengthening Community Broadcasting Grant Opportunity will provide grant funding of up to $4 million (GST exclusive) for grant activities to eligible applicants to strengthen the First Nations community broadcasting sector. Program objectives include supporting the First Nations broadcasting and media sector to modernise and stabilise operations and supporting the First Nations broadcasting and media sector to deliver reliable, high quality, culturally and locally relevant broadcasting services. The intended outcomes of the grant are: Improved capacity of First Nations broadcasting and media services to deliver high quality broadcasting services. Relevant First Nations news, information, cultural and educational programs remain accessible. Opportunities for training and development in the First Nations Broadcasting and Media sector are provided. Increase in the number of First Nations community broadcasting services operating in Australia.
